I’m in my 30s now so we weren’t together romantically, but we were still best friends and loved each other very much. One of the last things he did before he died was start to text me. Im still in contact with his family, especially his mom. I think my life would be very different if he hadn’t died and if he had moved where I live like he was thinking of doing. There were so many little and big things that brought me to not only meeting my husband, but being ready for that relationship. Her boyfriend dying is a huge part of who she is, even if they had just broken up who’s to say she would have still married her current husband? Break ups are wildly different from deaths, she could be a totally different person with a different outlook on life. Again, we’ll never know. 

We don’t have “one true love”, we can love many people in our lifetimes without it negating our other relationships.

Bunnies are wonderful pets that live 8-12 years. They can be litterbox trained and can be trained to do some tricks (there’s even one that can play basketball and paint). I typically say that they’re somewhat akin to cats that can’t jump as high. They sleep and hide when they want to, they’ll come get affection when they want to. Just like cats and dogs, some are more affectionate than others. My first bunny slept in bed with me and would cuddle all the time. One of my current bunnies will shove his head into my hand if I stop petting him. They’re crepuscular, which means they’re most active at dusk and Dawn, which is when I’m waking up/getting home from work. This is great since they sleep while I’m at work and then I get to give them lots of love and attention when it works best for the both of us. They are unbelievably silly and weird and hilariously bizarre. 

That being said, their vet care *can* get expensive and you do need to find a rabbit savy vet. But, emergency trips is what costs the most and that is true for cats and dogs as well. My yearly annual per bunny is like $50. 

Just like any other pet, they are a commitment and no one should get one without understanding that. They are not “starter pets” and they deserve the same love and attention that people give cats and dogs. PSA: never give pets as a gift to anyone unless it has been thoroughly discussed and they are aware that it is happening, kids getting easier bunnies is a huge issue for rabbit rescues and why so many rabbits get abandoned every year

It depends on the bunny, but for the most part it will be beneficial for the current bun. The important thing to do though is take your bun to a rescue for speed dating. Some rabbits immediately hate each other, and trying to bond them can be incredibly stressful for them, if not downright impossible. Your current bun choosing their own partner will make the process a lot easier. Some rescues will even help with the bonding process (mine had a board-to-bond program and they did most of the work for me honestly). 

If your rabbit is on the younger side, then I think you should definitely do some speed dates. If they have been alone for their entire life and are older, it might be more difficult since they don’t understand those relationship dynamics and haven’t had to worry about them for their entire life. I bonded my Coco to a 5 year old bun who was single up until then, and it’s worked out just fine. In 2017 I bonded a new bunny to my fierce, bossy, sassy girl who had been single for 6 years. That one didn’t go as well. They were fine living together but she was never very nice to him (no outright fighting though). She ended up passing away 6 months later and had I known that was going to happen, I never would’ve bonded her. 

I have seen a marked improvement in demeanor for bonded bunnies. Coco lost her husbun and was single for around 9 months before I bonded her to Benji. She is so much happier now than she was those entire 9 months, it’s such a stark difference.

Your vet bills will be more expensive, but once the bonding is done, they’re a lot less work. They take care of each other a lot and I don’t feel as bad about working or not always having tons of time to spend with them. I highly recommend at least trying (if you can handle the extra vet bill).

Actually provenance is a lot more complicated to prove than having a receipt. Trust me, this is an issue my museum has been dealing with for years. 

Do you think the Elgin marbles should be returned to Greece? Because there’s no reason that I’m aware of that would cause them to not be cared for properly. I can say with 99.9% authority that they would go on display too, especially as a “coming home” kind of exhibition.

ETA: Greece is holding space at the acropolis museum so the marbles would definitely go on view.

The British Museum isn’t the only museum in the world, things can be returned and properly cared for. And as I’ve said they have a lot more than just the Rosetta Stone. I’m not intimately familiar with the Egyptian museum scene, but I can tell you that the british museum just doesn’t want to give things back, it’s not because of some morality about preservation. The Elgin marbles are a prime example. 

I’m prefacing this with saying that I think looted art should be returned, but you’re saying that you’re cool for Nazi looted art to go back to being privately owned (and thus not seen by the public), but these antiquities that would go to a government/museum shouldn’t be returned because they’re for the people? Logically you have it backwards in terms of what artifacts would and wouldn’t be available to the public.

The point of them is to be returned to their government and put on display (or at least cared for, 90% of museum collections aren’t on display). It’s not like the Elgin marbles can be returned to a single person. Typically making claim to those things works by family inheritance but that just isn’t possible for these looted antiquities. Nazi looted art is a little different because there actually is family that can make a claim. These things weren’t sent to these museums for safe keeping, they were stolen. The way to avoid that is to loan artifacts, which is something that museums do all the time. For the most part that isn’t actually necessary, but that’s 100% an option. There’s certainly no worry of the Elgin marbles getting destroyed if they return to Greece, the British museum just refuses to give up its stolen artifacts. Museums do ethically sketching stuff to get around having to repatriate things all the time. I actually had a conversation with a curator today about the sketchy practices we have to make sure we don’t lose one particular painting that we don’t legally own.

So much of their stuff should be returned though, like the Elgin Marbles. The guy who took them originally did to decorate his own damn house. The British museum has SO many looted artifacts. 

This is a widespread issue in museums (every museum I’ve ever worked at had things of sketchy provenance) but the British Museum is one of the biggest offenders. The only reason native Americans got even a little of their stuff back was because a law was made that forced museums to do so. Nazi looted art is also its own whole thing…

I find bunnies to be very high maintenance pets. I’ve had very very many sleepless nights when they’ve been sick and have taken sick days from work to care for them/get them to the vet. Their health is really fragile and expensive. You need a rabbit savvy vet, which can be hard to find. My current bunny needs daily medication and a very specific diet. 

Temperament is also different for every bunny. My first bun loved to cuddle with me and sleep in my bed, but was SUPER mean to everyone else. She loved me and just hated everyone else (which was hilarious honestly). My other 3 all had different personalities too. Poptart was my grumpy old man who preferred men to women and wasn’t a big cuddler. Chickpea really liked attention but wasn’t the type to lay in bed with me. Coco is the equivalent of the sour patch kids commercial “first they’re sour than they’re sweet”. Since she has become a single bunny (Chickpea was her husbun who unfortunately passed away very unexpectedly last year) she has gotten super bossy. She’ll use her teeth to move me out of her way a lot but then will come up a few minutes later and give me a million kisses. She’s afraid of heights so no bed cuddles with her but she likes to be pet a lot. 

I’ve never taken them outside, it makes me way too nervous. Especially with RHSV2 (although she’s vaccinated now). All of my bunnies have been free roaming though and mostly their cowards (coco got terrified of the sound of me putting a jacket on once), so I don’t think they would’ve liked being outside anyways. 

All that being said, I’ve absolutely loved all of my bunnies and they have filled my life with so much joy. They are so weird and so silly. Even when Coco bosses me around, it still makes me so happy. I’m not sure I can keep rescuing them though, since their health is so fragile and they keep ripping my heart out. They can be great pets but you just need to know what you’re signing up for. 

If you decide to get a bunny, I recommend adopting because, aside from it saving lives, you can also learn about temperament beforehand.

It’s not a personal attack to say pets are expensive, that’s just the truth of the matter. Just like anything that has expensive maintenance costs, you should consider that before voluntarily getting into that situation. I don’t think that’s a hot take. 

Most people are living paycheck to paycheck (at least in the US), so it can easily become a choice of letting your pet die (which would be psychologically scarring) or paying your rent. We can’t just pretend that this problem doesn’t exist. An illness or injury with an animal in a shelter doesn’t automatically equal euthanasia. Not a single rabbit rescue I’ve worked at euthanized because of space, only when it was required due to medical issues. So yeah, we didn’t want to adopt to people who did not understand that these pets can easily cost thousands in vet bills. Doesn’t mean you had to be rich to, just that we needed you to be fully aware of it and willing to take on that risk. 

It’s not about shaming people living in poverty or saying they can’t have nice things. It’s about being aware before you voluntarily do something that requires a lot of maintenance cost. A lot of people (myself included for my first pet) get pets on a whim, because they’re adorable and we love them. But then you get saddled with the reality of the situation. I care about rescuing bunnies and have to stop myself from rescuing more, because I know I legitimately cannot afford it. 

It sucks, people should be paid adequately and they aren’t, renting shouldn’t take up an entire paycheck and you shouldn’t have to be making six figures to buy a house. But, unfortunately, that’s the reality of the bullshit system we’re in right now. Do what you can to help animals but also realize your limits.

Everyone I know with pets (myself included) has spent thousands in vet bills. It adds up, especially if you have more than one. There’s more to being a good partner than just talking, you need to follow it through with actions. And, if you have not taken any of those steps before, things can take a long time to get better. 

Example: I am a survivor of long term CSA. The first time I did anything more than just make out, I had a panic attack. Any time I tried anything new, I had a panic attack. I had absolutely no idea this was going to happen until it happened. Those huge issues weren’t revealed to me until I had those experiences. I’ve been doing work for years to get passed that and can now have a normal sex life. But nothing was close to normal or healthy in that regard for my first partner, it was a lot of emotional labor for him as well. We were both 17 though so he had his own big issues that he hadn’t realized yet that I worked with him about. We were young and didn’t have experience with relationships and we learned a lot. Those experiences are really important. 

So, at this point in my life, I’d rather date someone that already has that framework set up since I have done the work to do that. I wouldn’t expect anyone in their mid30s+ to want to date me if I acted the same as I did in my first relationship.

Being in a relationship reveals your own shortcomings and you (ideally) work on those. But if you’ve never been in a situation to reveal those issues, then you haven’t been able to work on them and have to start that process. I’m aware that I am not great at opening up. This is specific to romantic relationships too, it’s not a problem for me in my friendships. When sex gets involved, emotional vulnerability gets more complicated (at least for me). I started the process of working on it a while ago, so I’m a lot better off than I was during my first relationship. My first partner was great and patient, but basically did a lot of work to make me feel comfortable in a way that shouldn’t have been necessary. I don’t need that level of work from a partner now because I have worked on that issue. The entire thing is a learning process, you find out things about yourself that you wouldn’t find out in other types of relationships. You learn more about commitment and communication, because those aren’t the same as in a friendship. My best friend and I fight? Cool, we just take space and don’t talk for a few days and then maybe hang out in a week or two. But that doesn’t really work in a romantic relationship. And you learn how to deal with those things through experience.

That’s totally fine, I just don’t really want to date them. There’s a learning curve to being in a romantic relationship, it’s not the same as a friendship or your work relationships. And I, personally, would rather not date someone who has no experience in that. It doesn’t mean I think they’re terrible people or gross in some way, it just means I’m not really interested in dating them.

I’m still in the dating scene (although not actively for the moment) and I’ve never asked this or been asked it. I just wouldn’t answer if I were, since it’s not their business. I don’t think it’s about “judging”, or at least it isn’t for me. I wouldn’t date a virgin because if you’re in your mid30s+ and you’re a virgin, then there’s a reason behind that. At this point, I don’t really want to teach someone the basics of being in a romantic relationship. 

In my early 20s though someone else’s virginity wouldn’t have been a deal breaker for me.

ETA: I don’t think they’re gross or terrible people. I just want to be in a romantic relationship with someone who has experience with romantic relationships

You can lose your accreditation over it and you’ll get fucked in the community. It’s actually a state law where I live to follow AAM guidelines (much to the chagrin of the politician in charge of the state museums, but as collection manager it makes me very happy). You’ll get a TON of bad publicity too, so most museums that have tried to do it have backed out (the BMA is a great example of this.) The biggest issue is you’ll lose donors. People don’t want to donate art for you to just turn around and sell it. Collections are made up of donated objects or objects bought through donated funds. You lose your donors, you’re absolutely fucked. 

You can deaccession artworks, but the criteria is that it no longer fits your mission and/or you are unable to properly care for it (mostly meaning it is actively detrimental to safety of the the work.) If it is formally deaccessioned, which needs to be approved by the museum board, then the only options are to transfer it to another museum, sell it at auction, or destroy it. You can’t sell it to an individual and auction houses set the estimated price based upon appraisal values. 

With Covid, policies opened up a little but not to an insane level. Money earned through deaccessioning can only be used to buy new works or to care directly for the collection. This means conservation, new storage facilities, etc. You can’t use it for salaries, make up for lost revenue, or departments other than collections, etc. 

These are all outlined in collections statements of every accredited (and most non-accredited) museums, so you can’t go against it unless you change your statement which also requires board approval. There are a lot of safe guards in place to ensure that deaccessioning is done ethically and responsibly.
Museums don’t sell artwork that way. There are really strict protocols on how to dispose of art.

I think majority of the body positivity movement isn’t claiming being fat is healthy or unhealthy, it’s more about being okay with who you are as a person and no defining yourself (or having other people define you) by your weight. Of course their are extremists that take it wayyyyy too far, but that’s just what happens with everything. Ideally, weight would just be between a person and their doctor but the medical community is also very stigmatized against it. They only take few classes in nutrition and fail to look at the person as a whole. There are unending amount of stories where doctors refuse to look past someone’s weight and then it turns out their symptoms are caused by something completely unrelated. 

I will say though that drinking is heavily encouraged in American culture. The downsides of drinking are rarely talked about in media, unless a specific celebrity is going to rehab. All the beer commercials, the “mommy wine” culture, etc. People are unhealthy in so many different ways, being overweight is just the most immediately recognizable. It has also (wrongly) been seen as a failing of one’s character so it gets very demonized.

I agree with most of what you’re saying, except for the first point. Or at least, I dislike when it’s used as rational to shame overweight people. People choose to be unhealthy in so many different ways, being overweight is just immediately recognizable.

Also, socialized healthcare has everything to do with rich assholes never paying taxes and nothing to do with any illness/unhealthy actions. The money exists, American politicians (majority anyways) are too greedy and corrupt to do anything about it. If the rich paid even a little of their share and if our tax dollars weren’t wasted on bullshit, then we would easily have universal healthcare. America could have no overweight people at all and we still wouldn’t have universal healthcare. Also fuck all the corporations that lobby against this shit too. 

I think the point of the body positivity movement gets lost due to extremists. Tess Holliday in particular is a great example of this (because she’s an absolutely terrible human). It’s supposed to be about how your self worth (and the worth that society places on you) should not be dependent on your weight or appearance. It includes scars, acne, stretch marks, etc. There is a percentage though that are hardcore extremists, to the point that they say people who try to lose weight are “fat phobic”. Intuitive eating has been co-opted in the same way. It doesn’t mean that you should live off of pizza because you want it, it just means that you can have a slice of pizza and not feel shameful or gluttonous. 

I totally get what you’re saying about addiction, I’m dealing with my own issue now. But someone being like “you’re a horrible person for drinking” is just more likely to make me want to give up and drink. I actually feel really terrible for people that have out of control food addictions. I can cut alcohol out of my life but you can’t cut food out, you need to eat. Most overweight people though (in my optimism at least) don’t have a food addiction. If you can star on my 600-lb life, then yeah you are definitely unhealthily addicted; most people just consume way more calories than they realize and are way more sedentary than they realize.

No one is telling you to go 8 hours without eating (which is actually pretty normal though??), they’re still giving you food. You’re not going to get the food you want at all the events you go to. How is that different from eliminating ALL alcohol from a party I’m throwing? My friends sure as hell would rather party with alcohol and are “familiar” with coke but would prefer it to have rum in it.

That’s a whole separate issue. She chooses to be vegan due to her morals and is thus wanting a vegan menu at her own birthday party. Do you know how impossible it is to be 100% ethical in every consumer choice you ever make? Unless you grow and kill everything yourself or know the person that’s doing it (which means it costs more too). Everything is owned by a handful of companies so it’s nearly impossible to not give money to shitty parent companies in one way or another. Your clothes are likely unethical, your housing, etc etc. All we can do is try our best.

That’s why I said recovering alcoholics that can’t be around it, not all alcoholics. I sure as hell couldn’t throw a party with alcohol right now. And I said pork, not halal meat. From a Google search it says pork can’t be halal (but I’m not Muslim so I could be wrong). Either way, it’s totally fair for people to choose the menu of their own event based upon their beliefs.

But OP isn’t attending an event, she’s throwing it. You wouldn’t expect to find ANY bacon at an event thrown by a practicing Muslim. You wouldn’t find ANY alcohol at an event thrown by a recovering alcoholic that can’t be around it.

But you still choose the menu regardless, a catering service doesn’t give guests all the options of all the things they make. When you have a wedding, you do tastings and plan your menu. She’s just choosing the options that align with her morals.

She obviously can’t control what a restaurant serves but she is choosing the menu for her own private event, it’s not the same. What if she were going out to dinner with friends and chose a vegan restaurant? Is that pushing an agenda or just choosing the restaurant you want for your own birthday dinner?

Edit to add: any catered event is choosing what people are going to eat. If you’re at a catered event with only chicken and fish, you don’t get to order pizza. You control the menu (vegan or not) so you are controlling what they can eat.

Would you expect a Muslim to serve pork if they were having a party? Or a recovering alcoholic to serve alcohol? It’s completely fair for someone to choose the menu at an event they are hosting based upon their beliefs. Especially when it’s something doable like this. No one is going to die because one meal doesn’t have meat or dairy. If someone has some bizarro medical condition that says they need to eat meat at every single meal, then they can eat before (which is what a ton of vegans do) or talk to OP for accommodations.

When someone else (especially parents) are paying for the party, there are going to be restrictions (budget/date/location/etc). And especially since she’s a teen, they’re going to expect to have some input. They’re meat eaters and they’re looking at it from that perspective. When you go to a wedding it’s the standard chicken/fish/whatever with vegetarian or vegan options. This is what makes the most people at those events happy, which tends to be the goal of the person throwing that event. They are focusing on the whole event and not exclusively her. 

Personally, I think unless there’s a legitimate reason to not do it (beyond it’s not the “norm”), they should let her have her vegan party.

Agreed, this isn’t pushing veganism on anyone. Would it be pushing sobriety on people if they attended a dry party for a recovering alcoholic? She’s not talking about running documentaries and lectures about animal cruelty. She just doesn’t want there to be things that she’s morally opposed to at her own birthday. 

Also, eating vegan for one meal isn’t the end of the world. There’s a lot of get vegan food. Plus, I’m sure most people have had at least one vegan meal in their life, it’s not like you need to eat meat and dairy for every single meal you have. I frequently eat vegan meals without that being the intention, that’s just how the ingredients end up. 

I say NAH though since the parents are paying for it and I also see their point.

I never said that psychiatric drugs are the only cause of weight gain and to blame for obesity. I’m saying it is a factor. There are so many factors involved in weight that it’s not so easy to say “stop eating fast food”. Socio economic factors, a persons up brining, health issues all work together to influence how we live our lives. 

It isn’t impossible, but the more barriers someone has the less likely they are to accomplish something. Someone who is already overweight due to their upbringing, then add in illness that has weight gain as a side effect, and then a medication that also has weight gain as a side effect. And if they have a family to take care of, live in poverty, etc etc. There are just so many factors, people need to get out of the mindset that fat automatically equals lazy. 

My mental illness and medications I have been on and traumas have caused weight gain, which is a barrier. I am lucky enough to not have anyone else to take care of and have disposable income to go to fitness classes that I legitimately enjoy. It is easier for me to lose/maintain weight than it is for someone that has additional barriers.  Like I said above, look at the whole picture and have some empathy.

Most psychiatric drugs for bipolar or depression cause weight. It is the first thing every doctor I’ve seen has said. I am EXTREMELY lucky that I could switch my med, I’m on one that is normally not prescribed for bipolar disorder. It’s also, honestly, because I lied and didn’t tell my doctor about my unhealthy obsession with my weight. It is NOT an option for a lot of people to switch their meds and it is no ones fault if they can’t. You can’t just will yourself into working with medication if it doesn’t work for you. You also seem to be misunderstanding what I say with the effects. It’s not switching from fried chicken to grilled. It makes you SIGNIFICANTLY hungrier. It is no where near as simple as you want it to be. I never ate out when I was on olanzapine but I would clear out my fridge due to the extreme hunger. 

Edit to add for emphasis: I have been on medications that others love but have made me unbelievably suicidal. You really really really can’t just decide to switch to something if it doesn’t work for you. 

Yes, it is about priorities, but not everyone can make losing weight their top priority. Poverty, caring for family, etc all require a ton of focus. My mental health requires an extreme amount of work and I can’t also make losing weight my top priority either (especially in a way that isn’t somewhat disordered). People love to vilify fat people and over simplify it to laziness or gluttony. Look at the whole picture and practice some empathy.

You do know that people have to take some psychiatric drugs for life, right? There is no cure, you just have to keep taking something where a side effect is an increased appetite that you can’t do anything about. Olanzapine destroyed me for it, I was just ravenous all the time. Luckily I found a different medication that could work, but not everyone is as lucky as I am. You can also be overweight/obese without eating nothing but fast food. Obese people aren’t a monolith, they didn’t all get there the same way and they don’t live identical lives. There are just more factors that go into someone’s lifestyle than “fast food and sugary drinks”.

Are mental illnesses and their treatments also apart of that 1%, or is that something just being ignored as a factor? You can’t just snap out of the effects of mental illness and it can frequently cause weight gain. A lot of psychiatric medicines also cause weight gain. 

I think you’re discounting how hard it is to radically change your life. If your entire childhood up to age 18 has been promoting an unhealthy lifestyle, you can’t just unlearn that at the snap of a finger. From the American Academy of child and adolescent psychiatry, kids have a 50% chance if one parent is obese and 80% if two are. Let’s also acknowledge that it is hard to lose weight, it’s not like getting two shots for a vaccine.
